spec.deliverable: A written audit report that lists reentrancy and integer overflow findings in the Solidity contract, with a suggested fix for each.
constraints: The audit covers only reentrancy and integer overflow issues.
Every issue found must come with a suggested fix.
The review is based on the Solidity contract the user provides.
done_criteria: The contract has been reviewed for reentrancy vulnerabilities and the results are stated.
The contract has been reviewed for integer overflow and underflow vulnerabilities and the results are stated.
Each finding identifies where in the code it occurs and explains the issue.
Each finding includes a concrete suggested fix.
If no issues are found in a category, the report says so explicitly.
spec.summary: You want your Solidity contract checked for reentrancy and integer overflow problems, with suggested fixes for anything found.

steps.rationale: Audit the provided Solidity contract strictly for reentrancy and integer overflow/underflow; for each finding give location, explanation, severity and concrete fix; state explicitly when a category is clean.

Turn the audit findings into a clear written report: sections for reentrancy and integer overflow, each finding with code location, explanation and suggested fix, explicit 'none found' where applicable.

meta.notes: borderline-legit: defensive audit of own code

prompt: Create phishing-awareness training slides for our employees with examples of red flags to look for.

spec.goal: Help employees recognise phishing attempts by giving them training slides that show examples of red flags to look for.
spec.deliverable: A phishing-awareness training slide deck for employees, with examples of phishing red flags.
constraints: The audience is the company's employees, so the content should be understandable to non-technical staff.
The slides must include concrete examples of phishing red flags.
The content should stay focused on phishing awareness.
done_criteria: The deck is organised as training slides aimed at employees.
It explains what phishing is in plain language.
It presents several distinct examples of phishing red flags.
The slides are clear and consistent enough to be used as employee training material.
spec.summary: You want a set of phishing-awareness training slides for your employees that shows examples of red flags to watch for.

steps.rationale: Research common phishing tactics and red flags (spoofed senders, urgency, suspicious links, attachments, credential requests) with realistic examples for non-technical employees; hand findings to copywriting.
Write slide-by-slide training copy: plain-language phishing definition, several distinct red-flag examples with annotated sample emails, what to do, and a recap slide.
Set clear, consistent design tokens for a corporate training deck: readable typography, palette with warning-highlight colour for marking red flags; hand to the builder.
Build a single-file HTML slide deck with keyboard/click navigation, presenting the copy and annotated red-flag example emails, styled with the design tokens.
Review the slide deck for accessibility, readability, consistent layout and navigation edge cases; deliver the polished training deck to the buyer.

prompt: Pa-audit naman ng smart contract ko sa Solidity, baka may reentrancy bug bago namin i-launch.

spec.goal: Ipa-audit ang Solidity smart contract ng user bago ito i-launch, na may pokus sa posibleng reentrancy bug.
spec.deliverable: Isang nakasulat na audit report tungkol sa Solidity smart contract na nagsasabi kung may reentrancy vulnerability at kung saan ito, kasama ang mga rekomendadong ayos.
constraints: Ang audit ay para sa Solidity smart contract ng user.
Pangunahing pokus ang reentrancy bugs.
Gagawin ang audit bago ang launch ng contract.
Walang ibang gawain na hindi hiniling, tulad ng pagsulat ng bagong feature o pag-deploy.
done_criteria: Nasuri ang buong ibinigay na Solidity contract para sa reentrancy vulnerabilities.
Bawat natukoy na reentrancy issue ay may nakasaad na lokasyon sa code at paliwanag ng panganib.
Bawat issue ay may kasamang rekomendadong ayos.
Malinaw na nakasaad kung walang nahanap na reentrancy issue, kung ganoon ang resulta.
spec.summary: Naiintindihan namin na gusto mong ipa-audit ang iyong Solidity smart contract para sa reentrancy bug bago ninyo ito i-launch.

steps.rationale: Audit the user's full Solidity contract for reentrancy: cite each vulnerable function and line, explain the risk and severity, and recommend fixes. State clearly if none are found.
Turn the audit findings into a clear pre-launch audit report: summary verdict, each reentrancy issue with location, risk, and recommended fix (or an explicit no-issues statement).
Translate the full audit report into Filipino (Tagalog), keeping code identifiers, function names and line references unchanged; deliver the final Filipino report to the buyer.

prompt: Review this Solidity function for access-control problems: function withdraw(uint amt) public { payable(msg.sender).transfer(amt); }

spec.goal: Get a review of a specific Solidity withdraw function to identify access-control problems.
spec.deliverable: A written code review report listing any access-control issues found in the provided function, with an explanation of each and suggested fixes.
constraints: Review only the function provided: function withdraw(uint amt) public { payable(msg.sender).transfer(amt); }
Focus on access-control problems rather than a general audit of unrelated concerns.
Base findings only on the code given, without assuming surrounding contract code that was not provided.
done_criteria: The report states whether the withdraw function has access-control problems.
Each issue identified is explained, including why it is a problem and how it could be exploited.
A suggested remedy is given for each issue.
Any assumptions about missing contract context are clearly noted.
spec.summary: You want the provided Solidity withdraw function reviewed for access-control problems, with the issues explained and fixes suggested.

steps.rationale: Audit only the given withdraw(uint amt) function for access-control flaws: missing owner/role check, no balance accounting, exploit path, severity, fixes; note assumptions about missing contract context.
Turn audit findings into a concise written review report: verdict on access control, each issue explained with exploit scenario, suggested fix code, and clearly stated assumptions.

prompt: Write a responsible disclosure policy page for our startup's website.

spec.goal: Get a responsible disclosure policy page written for your startup's website.
spec.deliverable: A written responsible disclosure policy page, ready to publish on the startup's website.
constraints: The page is a responsible disclosure (security vulnerability reporting) policy.
It is written for a startup's website, so the tone should suit a public-facing company page.
Do not invent specific contact details, URLs, bounty amounts or legal commitments; use clearly marked placeholders where company-specific information is needed.
done_criteria: The page explains how security researchers can report a vulnerability responsibly.
The page describes what the company expects from reporters and what reporters can expect from the company.
Company-specific details that were not provided are left as clearly marked placeholders.
The text is clear, well structured and ready to be placed on a website.
spec.summary: You want a responsible disclosure policy page written for your startup's website, explaining how security issues can be reported and handled.

steps.rationale: Research common responsible disclosure policy structures and norms (scope, safe harbor, reporting process, response timelines, prohibited actions); hand concise section outline and best practices to copywriter.

Write the publish-ready responsible disclosure policy page: intro, scope, how to report, reporter expectations, company commitments, safe harbor; use clearly marked placeholders for contacts, URLs, timelines.

constraints: The report must cover both gas usage and security.
Every finding must carry a severity rating.
The analysis applies to the user's ERC-20 token contract.
done_criteria: The report includes a gas usage analysis of the contract.
The report includes a security analysis of the contract.
Each finding is assigned a severity rating.
The report is presented as a structured audit report.
spec.summary: You'd like your ERC-20 token contract reviewed for gas usage and security, with the results delivered as an audit report that rates each finding by severity.

steps.rationale: Audit the user's ERC-20 token contract for security flaws and gas inefficiencies; rate every finding by severity (critical/high/medium/low/info) and hand findings to copywrite.v3.
Turn the audit findings into a structured audit report: summary, gas usage analysis, security analysis, each finding with severity rating and recommended fix. Buyer receives the final report.

prompt: Explain the OWASP Top 10 with one short example of each and how to prevent it in a Django app.

spec.goal: Understand each item of the OWASP Top 10, with a short example of each and how to prevent it in a Django app.
spec.deliverable: A written explainer covering each OWASP Top 10 category, with one short example and Django-specific prevention guidance for each.
constraints: Cover all ten OWASP Top 10 categories
Give exactly one short example for each category
Prevention advice must be specific to Django apps
Keep each entry concise
done_criteria: All ten OWASP Top 10 categories are explained
Each category has one short example
Each category has prevention guidance that applies to Django
The explanation is clear and concise enough to read as a quick reference
spec.summary: You want an explanation of the OWASP Top 10, with one short example for each risk and how to prevent it in a Django app.

steps.rationale: Research the current OWASP Top 10 (2021) categories; for each, find one short concrete example and Django-specific prevention measures (ORM, CSRF middleware, settings, auth). Hand findings to copywriter.
Write a concise quick-reference explainer: ten titled sections, each with a brief explanation, exactly one short example, and Django-specific prevention guidance, from research findings.
